offers.name: Lenovo Legion 5 16" WQXGA 240Hz Gaming Laptop - Intel Core Ultra 9 275HX - 32GB DDR5 - 1TB SSD - RTX 5060 - Windows 11 Home - Gray

reviews.quote: It's built well and clean looking, offers solid ergonomics, decent inputs ... the mid-range RTX 5060/5070 options are the ones to look at, as they are priced competitively and can be properly tamed in this chassis.

professional.note: No pro review found for the Legion 5 16 Gen 10 IPS config (honest disclosure per SHARED-legion5-ips.md); inferred from Pro 5 16 Gen 10 (86.8%) and Legion 5 15 chassis (87%).

praises: 24-core Ultra 9 275HX + 32GB RAM makes this the workstation spec of the 16" Legion 5 line at a sale price well under its $5,149 list
240Hz 16" WQXGA matte IPS: buttery motion, ~500 nits, zero PWM flicker
UltrabookReview: the 5060/5070 tiers 'can be properly tamed in this chassis' — good sustained clocks without extreme fan noise
Dual SODIMM to 64GB and dual M.2 — future-proof without warranty hassle
Wi-Fi 7, 5MP webcam with eShutter, full-size numpad keyboard praised across the chassis family (NBC: 'very comfortable')
complaints: GPU/RAM pairing still skewed: for pure gaming, a 5070 config elsewhere is better FPS per dollar
~2.4 kg / 25 mm — this is a desk-first laptop; the 15" Legion 5s travel much better
No Thunderbolt on Intel Legion 5 models; no card reader (NBC cons)
Legion platform threads: warranty friction (LENOVEO), occasional fan-bearing grind and 50-series driver crashes on some units

standouts: 32GB + 24-core CPU + 240Hz 16" at $3,599 sale — the best all-round 16" spec of the non-OLED Legion 5 range
design_philosophy: The 32GB twin of the 16" Legion 5 Gen 10 fixes the entry tier's one real gap: it matches the desktop-class CPU with enough memory for heavy multitasking, VMs, or local LLM tinkering, while keeping the cool-running 5060 and the big 240Hz matte panel. It is the 'gamer who also works' configuration of the line.
